name: חֲנָנִי
gloss: he has been gracious to me; or my grace
summary: Read as the verb with “me”, “he has been gracious to me”, a short form of Hananiah. Borne by Hanani the seer, who rebuked Asa for relying on the king of Aram and not on Yahweh and was put in prison (2Ch 16:7–10), father of the prophet Jehu (1Ki 16:1, 7; 2Ch 19:2; 20:34); a son of Heman the singer (1Ch 25:4, 25); a priest of the sons of Immer who had taken a foreign wife (Ezr 10:20); Nehemiah's brother, who brought word of Jerusalem's broken wall and was given charge over the city (Neh 1:2; 7:2); and a musician at the dedication of the wall (Neh 12:36).

evidence.note: “Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said, Because you relied on the king of Aram and did not rely on Yahweh your God.”
“Hanani, one of my brothers, came, he and men of Judah.”
The verb with “me”: “for God חַנַּנִי (has dealt graciously with me)”.

note: Takes h.dz.an (11 tokens). TIPNR counts the seer of 2Ch 16:7 with the father of Jehu (Hanani@1Ki.16.1). The reading “he has been gracious to me” takes the form as the verb with a suffix, as חַנַּנִי (Gen 33:11); it may also be the adjectival ending, “gracious”. No verse gives the meaning.
